answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks with bonded reputation: every agent locks a collateral stake to register, and peers attest its on-chain behavior. A sybil farm costs one stake per clone, capital locked in escrow and multiplied by N, and any cluster flagged for coordination is slashed, its bond paid to honest verifiers. Trust scores use ridge regression so genuine agents stay on one sharp ridge while duplicates collapse into correlated noise. The top tier is an ivory bond: an expensive, non-transferable escrow whose slashing lights a lantern on the ledger for all future verifiers.
